title: Bean Root Rot (Caused by Pythium) - Rwanda

Header: Bean Root Rot (Caused by Pythium) - Rwanda
Pythium ultimum Indwara z'imizi in Kinyarwanda

Prevention: Avoid planting beans in acidic soil (lime application two weeks before planting 5 tonnes per hectare).
Use fertilizers to help plants be more vigorous, basal application organic fertilizer 20-30ton/Ha and
Crop rotation with cereal, root and tuber crops.
Use resistant / tolerant varieties such as
G3331, Vuninkingi (G685), RWV2872, RWV3316, RWV3006, RWR2245, RWR2154.
Do not over irrigate the bean crop.
Avoid overwatering in the early stage of crop development.
Control movement of water across plantations through soil erosion control.
Monitoring: Monitor fields 4-7 days after planting until the 3rd trifoliate leaf (V3 stage).
Check for wilt and yellow leaves on the bean plants.
Look for elongated, narrow lesions or spots on the hypocotyls.
The spots or lesions first to appear are reddish purple in colour then they become black because of the wet soft rot.
Primary and secondary roots are rotted and root system is destroyed.
Look for leaves that have turned yellow or have dropped off and died.
Uproot to assess if the roots are rotten (wet rot).
Direct Control: Uproot if infected 1-2 weeks after seedling emergence.
Restrictions: Do not eat or drink while manipulating pesticide.
